As the province’s largest energy provider with more than 100 years of knowledge and experience, we proudly deliver renewable energy, natural gas, electricity and propane to 1.3 million customers.

We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. As one of BC's Top Employers with a diverse team of over 2,700 employees, we are committed to a safe and inclusive culture where each of us can connect, belong, and grow. Join us, and together, let's shape a brighter future for B.C.

Position Overview

You’re a sharp analytical thinker with a knack for leveraging utility planning optimization software tools. Along with your love for quantitative analysis, you’re a numbers guru who excels in forecasting and modelling analyses.

In this role, you will:


Ensure the execution of strategies at the departmental and organizational level, both for analytical and regulatory submissions, that support business priorities.
Strengthen internal modelling expertise and capabilities while strategically guiding and integrating third-party consultant analyses into resource planning activities.
Analyze markets, energy utility planning environment, customer energy use, and provide useful qualitative and comparative insights.
Support workshops between our Gas and Electric utility resource planning analyses and reporting activities.
Collaborate with internal and external cross-functional experts to use energy demand and other business data to support recommendations on planning and project strategies.


What it takes:


A degree in economics, computer science, finance, business administration, or a related resource development field.
A minimum of four years of related analytical experience.
A demonstrated ability to learn coding languages such as R, Python, or other.
Prior experience with optimization models, production cost analytics, and macroeconomic modeling through software such as Plexos, Aurora, Navius, or other energy modelling tools is an asset.
Strong attention to detail and organization skills to conduct accurate analyses and forecasts.
Excellent interpersonal and time management skills to develop and deliver presentations with succinct recommendations and supported strategic arguments.


In this role, you will have the option to participate in a flexible work program, enabling you to work from an approved flex location in British Columbia up to 85 days a year (equivalent to approximately two days a week), subject to business or operational needs.

Our engaging workplace offers a wide range of challenging opportunities, while being safe, inclusive, and diverse. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, while supporting life-long career development. We also encourage volunteerism and nourish the need to give back to your community.

Title: Senior Systems Analyst (Senior Data Engineer and Analyst)
Description:
BCIT’s Information Technology Services department is seeking a regular, full-time (1.0 FTE) Senior Systems Analyst to participate in the ERP modernization initiatives. This position plays a key role as an experienced senior data engineer and analyst to design, develop, and support enterprise-scale data platforms and solutions.




The Senior Systems Analyst will be responsible for Microsoft Fabric, enterprise database, enterprise data warehouse, data factory, ETL pipelines, data conversion and migration initiatives, and providing business users with accurate, timely, and actionable insights through Power BI.




DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:




Development and Analysis:

Perform data analysis using PL/SQL or T-SQL to identify trends, anomalies, and data quality issues.
Collaborate with business stakeholders on data quality issues and gather business logic for remediation.
Participate in data modelling, develop complex PL/SQL or T-SQL scripts and stored procedures that will be used in Data Conversion.
Design, develop, and maintain enterprise data warehouse and modern data platform architectures in MS Fabric.
Develop scalable data ingestion and ETL pipelines to load data into centralized enterprise database and data warehouse.




Dashboard and Reporting:

Contribute to the planning, design, development, and deployment of new dashboards in Power BI.
Build scripts using DAX and Power Query for Power BI.




Documentation & Collaboration:

Collaborate with business users and functional analysts to gather requirements.
Use AI tools like Cursor or Claude to document data flows, transformations, and business rules to support transparency and sustainability.




QUALIFICATIONS:




Minimum two-year diploma in Computer Systems, Data Management, or a related discipline, or a bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, statistics, business, or related field; plus a minimum of six (6) years of current, practical experience, of which at least four (4) years must be in a similar role or a closely related data-focused role.
An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.
Effective oral and written communication skills.
Must have demonstrated specific current IT knowledge.
Proven commitment to providing and maintaining the highest level of customer service.
Proven analytical and problem-solving skills.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage changing priorities and meet deadlines.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team and with cross-departmental groups.
Ability to learn quickly and apply new knowledge and techniques.
Commitment to ongoing professional development.
High level of professionalism and ethical responsibility, particularly in the handling of institutional data.




Qualifications Specifics:

Proficiency Oracle PL/SQL or T-SQL, and stored procedures for querying, data manipulation, and analysis in large, complex databases environment.
Experience in MS Fabric platform including data factory, and One Lake.
Proficiency with DAX, Power Query and Microsoft Power BI.
Solid understanding of data governance principles, data quality, and data lifecycle management
Experience in enterprise or corporate data modeling with strong understanding of dimensional modelling, analytical data structures and reporting requirements
Experience with data analysis, profiling, and validation techniques
Experience designing and creating SSIS and executing ETL/ELT processes to support enterprise reporting and analytics platforms.
Familiarity with data integration tools, orchestration platforms, or pipelines used in enterprise environments.
Experience working in agile or hybrid delivery environments.




Nice-to-Have Qualifications:

Hands-on experience working with a post-secondary ERP, preferably Ellucian Banner ERP, including understanding of core data structures and functional modules.
Experience with Ellucian Ethos and Ethos Data Models.
Experience supporting Banner SaaS implementations or migrations.
Experience working with post-secondary institutional data standards and regulatory reporting.
Experience with data governance or metadata management tools.
Familiarity with JIRA or similar work management tools.
Experience with other analytics tools like Tableau, Ellucian Insights, and Argos.




SALARY:




Salary Range: $84,685 - $112,200 per annum.




Additional Salary Information: Salary prorated based on percentage and term of appointment. Salary based on education, experience and placement criteria as outlined in the Collective Agreement.




Benefits – Why you’d love working with us




Competitive pay
Minimum of twenty-five days of vacation (or more, depending on your position)
Competitive employer-paid extended health and dental plan – take a look at our benefit plans!
Defined benefit pension plan with employer contributions
Flexible hybrid work arrangements available
Professional Development funds and resources
Access to most BCIT Flexible Learning courses free of charge
Wellness and Employee Assistance programs
Complimentary membership with free access to the Fitness Centre, Gymnasium, and more

Title: Quantitative Analyst
Description:
Powerex Corp. is the wholly owned energy marketing subsidiary of BC Hydro, responsible for marketing clean electricity across North America. We are seeking an experienced Quantitative Analyst with a background in Operations Research to join our Analytics team. This role is ideal for someone who combines deep analytical expertise with strong programming skills and a passion for applying both to complex, real-world energy market problems. The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, self-driven, and comfortable delivering rigorous analysis in a fast-paced trading environment.

Reporting to the Director, Analytics, you will work closely with traders and senior analysts to support Front Office operations through mathematical modelling, deal valuation, data analysis, and tool development. Your primary function will be to support and maintain existing mathematical programming models and to develop new ones from concept to implementation. This position will be relied upon to support the achievement of our purpose and long-term goals by fostering our values: teamwork, accountability, integrity, service, ingenuity, and safety.

Key Responsibilities


Maintain and enhance existing mathematical programming models, ensuring reliability, accuracy, and alignment with evolving business needs
Design and develop new quantitative models from concept through to implementation, applying operations research techniques to real-world energy market problems
Perform deal valuation and quantitative analysis to support Front Office trading decisions
Build and maintain analytical tools and data pipelines that support trading operations and workflows
Conduct data analysis using large datasets, extracting insights that inform trading strategy and risk assessment
Collaborate with traders, analysts, and other stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into analytical solutions
Contribute to the continuous improvement of Front Office tools, models, and processes through innovation and automation
Produce clear technical documentation and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences
Support ad-hoc analytical requests while managing longer-term modelling projects in parallel



Qualifications

Required


Bachelor's degree in a field such as Engineering, Economics, Mathematics, or Statistics
At least five years of quantitative analytical work experience, a substantial portion of which has been specifically in operations research. Candidates without a formal operations research background will be considered provided they demonstrate sufficient quantitative and technical experience and aptitude
Demonstrated ability to solve challenging technical problems without the guarantee of adequate or perfect information, delivering both quick ad-hoc solutions and long-term in-depth models
Experience solving real-world problems by translating them into constraints represented by computer models
Strong grounding in probability and statistics, and the judgement to know which methods fit a given problem
Ability to explain quantitative reasoning to traders and commercial staff, and to defend it under challenge
Expert-level proficiency in MS Excel and at least one data visualization or dashboarding tool such as Tableau
Scripting experience in a mathematical programming language, ideally AMPL & CPLEX
Programming experience in at least one of VBA, Python, C++/C#, or SQL (Snowflake, dbt)
Proven experience working with large datasets and managing end-to-end data pipelines
Strong technical writing skills
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with both technical and business stakeholders
Ability to work independently, multi-task, and thrive under pressure in a fast-paced, open work environment



Preferred


A Master's degree in Operations Research or another analytical field, and/or successful completion of a professional development program such as a CFA
Experience in the energy industry
Experience working with LLMs such as Claude to support research and the development of tools, models, and data pipelines
Knowledge or experience in hydrology, hydropower engineering, time-series forecasting, or general data science



Work Arrangements & Other Requirements


Full-time, in-office position based at our Vancouver, BC office
Must be located in the Vancouver/Lower Mainland area
Must be legally authorized to work in Canada
A background check and references will be required for the position



What We Offer


Compensation: The expected salary range for this role is $109,680 - $148,400
Comprehensive benefits package including extended health, dental, vision, and pension
Opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced quantitative analysis and North America's energy markets, contributing directly to Front Office trading and decision-making
A collaborative, innovation-driven environment that embraces modern analytical tools, AI, and emerging technologies in energy trading
Professional development support, including funding for relevant certifications, training, and continuing education



About Powerex

Powerex Corp. is a market leader in the trading and marketing of clean and renewable wholesale electricity and associated environmental products. We are at the forefront of the clean energy transition, helping our wholesale customers throughout Western North America meet their increasingly ambitious environmental goals. Our customers include electricity and natural gas utilities, global energy companies, large financial institutions, and global technology companies. Powerex's financial success directly benefits British Columbians by helping to lower BC Hydro's electricity rates.

Fast paced, dynamic, and empowering are words that describe a career with Powerex. We pride ourselves on having a supportive and fun culture, and a strong commitment to the development and wellbeing of our employees. With an average tenure of 15+ years on our trade floor, Powerex stands out as an employer of choice in Vancouver. Ask any Powerex employee what they love about their job, and their first comment will likely be "the people I work with every day."

At Powerex we believe that a diverse team is a strong team, and our dedication to equity and inclusion is intertwined with our performance-based culture. We strive for excellence in everything we do, and we recognize that diverse perspectives and backgrounds fuel innovation and drive superior performance.

Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Title: Member Contact Operations Analyst (12-Month Contract and 20-Month Contract)
Description:
Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.

As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,300 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!

Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As a Member Contact Operations Analyst, you will play a key role in enabling the development of optimized business results through data-driven insights. You will define and translate business needs into actionable requirements, develop operational reports using real-time and historical data, and collaborate with stakeholders to deliver solutions that enhance member experience. We’re looking for a detail-oriented, analytical thinker who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is passionate about leveraging technology to improve processes. Experience in Genesys Cloud admin will be integral for success in this role. 

This is a Full-time, Temporary role based at our Surrey Central Office or from your B.C based home office under remote working arrangements. While this position provides a hybrid work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.

How You’ll Make an Impact:

Defining, analyzing and interpreting business needs into clear business requirements, user stories, and process models
Developing cross-functional reports using data from multiple sources to meet business needs
Identifying process or access changes required and communicating these to stakeholders
Collaborating with end users to create new or enhance existing report templates in conjunction with IT teams
Contributing to project deliverables in both agile and waterfall methodologies
Supporting design, build, test, training, and deployment phases of projects
Creating and maintaining documentation for reporting processes and actively managed documents
Managing end-user profiles and permissions on Genesys reporting platforms
Support Genesys Cloud admin, with an emphasis on A3S, Snowflake, App Foundry, Kibana etc.


What You’ll Bring to the Team:

At least 2 years of post-secondary education in a relevant field (e.g Database Admin, Data Analytics, Data Science)
Minimum 2+ years of experience in a contact center environment
1+ year back-end administrative experience with Genesys Cloud Platform
Minimum 1+ year of experience with Database Management Systems (e.g., Power BI, SQL)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
Self-driven persistence in conducting deep data analysis to gain a comprehensive understanding, uncover insights, and resolve discrepancies.
Ability to communicate effectively and translate business requirements into technical specifications


Extra Skills That Set You Apart:

Experience providing technical guidance or acting as a subject matter expert
Familiarity with agile and waterfall project methodologies
Creativity in developing reporting solutions and improving processes


You’ll Thrive Here If You Are:

An Analyzer & Problem Solver - Skilled at detecting anomalies and resolving discrepancies.
Solutions-focused & Process-oriented - Confident in decision-making and improving tools and processes.
A Communicator with Influence - Able to present data effectively and collaborate with stakeholders.
Self-starter - Proactive and motivated to meet timelines and deliverables.


What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of $55,300 to $65,000 per annum. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:

Living Wage Employer: We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers.
Customizable Benefits: Permanent employees receive flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet evolving needs.
Generous Vacation: New employees start with 3-4 weeks of vacation per year, with additional days earned over time.
Extra Stat Holidays: In addition to BC’s 11 statutory holidays, we offer 2 extra days, plus care days for personal or family illness.
Immediate Health Coverage: Health and dental benefits begin on your hire date, with three levels of coverage to choose from.
Defined Benefit Pension: Our retirement plan provides a guaranteed income for life, recognizing that retirement looks different for everyone.


Vancity Talent Programs:

Vancity supports an inclusive hiring process for candidates who self-identify as Indigenous, Black, or Trans. With special permission from the BC Human Rights Commissioner, this initiative provides access to career development opportunities, prioritized job screening, and feedback. Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). For details, please see our dedicated Talent Programs job posting.

At Vancity we’re committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace to help our people and communities thrive and prosper. Diversity in our workforce is integral so that we can truly represent, understand and respond to our community needs and deliver on our member experience.

We are also committed to an inclusive, barrier-free and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. We’re here to work with you to ensure your needs are met promptly and effectively. All requests will be handled with the utmost respect and confidentiality, so you can participate fully in the process.

Title: Quantitative Equity Analyst Process Engineering
Description:
We are looking for a Quantitative Equity Analyst to join our Quantitative Equity Team! We are a high-performance team embedded in a top-performing quantitative equity fund that manages over $78+ billion USD in financial assets. We are dedicated to the mission-critical operation of our investment engine—a well-tuned machine responsible for generating key decisions that drive trades and investment insights. Leveraging finance skills and cutting-edge technology, we ensure data quality, continuous process improvement, and operational excellence.

As a core member of our team, you'll collaborate with investment experts to tackle challenging analytical problems, be accountable to ensure accurate and timely trade generation, and drive operational innovation. Title: 26-61 Senior Business Intelligence Analyst (10 months)
Description:
The Opportunity

Supports the Leader in the strategy and operation of Technical Safety BC’s business intelligence program supporting driving operational efficiencies and measurement of organizational strategy implementation. Provides an advanced level of expertise in business intelligence to develop and deliver data and information products for internal and external customers and stakeholders. Independently carries out complex needs assessment, identifies opportunities to optimize use of data and information extracted from internal and external sources, and determines optimal methods to deliver resulting products to meet business needs. Provides day-to-day technical guidance to the Business Intelligence Analyst.

Status: Casual, Full-Time, Union

Number of Positions: 1

Pay Grade: (Grade 18) $61.87/hr

Location: Vancouver or open to any of our BC regional offices

Reports to: Leader, Business Intelligence

As a Senior Business Intelligence Analyst, you will:


Applies an advanced level of expertise in the strategy and operation of Technical Safety BC’s business intelligence program. Provides input to development of corporate strategies to influence change through data, information and knowledge, and participates in implementation and delivery.
Identifies information needs, including situations where clients cannot clearly articulate the need, available solutions fall short, and data is of lower quality. Designs, develops, and delivers complex data and information products that are scalable and accessible to internal and external customers through standard or unique reports and self-serve methods.
Leads and participates in data initiatives that are strictly speaking outside of Business Intelligence, including data definition, data modelling, data quality, information management, and records management.
Applies an advanced level of expertise in experimental design, applying creativity and exploring innovative solutions to address client-specific needs. Tests information products, evaluates findings, and redesigns as necessary to deliver required outcomes. Educates end users at senior levels of the organization on the proper use of BI products.
Supports the Leader in developing a framework of processes, practices and standards to ensure all product development and information sharing is executed with cost-effective, timely, and operationally efficient results. Develops ethical standards on the use of information within the organization. Fosters transparency and ready-access to information, while also establishing the necessary controls to mitigate risks.
Collaborates with the Information Technology and Data Management departments in identifying optimal solutions and delivering information services throughout the organization. Negotiates solutions and scheduling with IT/DM departments while maintaining excellent relationships with the IT/DM departments.
Collaborates with leaders to assess and advise on business intelligence needs, and determines optimal methods and products to support achievement of business objectives. Manages internal expectations and takes action to find common ground for differing agendas and conflicting objectives. Assesses and prioritizes day-to-day requests, applying judgement in the context of organization-wide requirements.
Collaborates with the Leader in providing communication and advice that encourages client behavioural change through use of data and information products. Appropriately addresses use of data and information that does not meet BCSA security, privacy, or ethical standards, with escalation to Leader or Director as necessary.
Supports the Leader in development of reports, presentations and business cases in support of business intelligence program initiatives.
Proactively resolves complex program issues and challenges (e.g. Operations), referring only the unresolved, escalated situations to the Leader for direction.
Conducts research and continuously maintains knowledge and awareness of the business intelligence practices, methods and related industry trends.
Provides day-to-day technical guidance to the Business Intelligence Analyst.



Knowledge, Skills & Experience you have:

Education And Experience

The required knowledge and skills for the position would typically be acquired through a Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or other related discipline and 6 - 8 years of experience in business intelligence in a measurement-intense environment, including experience working within IT teams in the delivery of BI solutions.

Achievement of (or eligible for) a relevant professional designation is also required.

Knowledge And Skills


Advanced practical knowledge of business intelligence concepts and solutions, use of external data, publishing open data, client-specific offerings, report and self-serve methods
Advanced ability to understand and transform user information needs into visually well-designed business intelligence products
Advanced understanding and application of experimental design, combined with creativity and curiosity to explore innovative solutions (evidenced by portfolio)
Advanced and diverse experience in implementing, deploying, and operating BI technology stacks.
Solid business acumen and ethics to assess business intelligence requirements and priorities in the context of differing agendas or conflicting objectives
Advanced understanding of IT systems, databases, and data management including data quality
Advanced communication and interpersonal skills to engage in collaborative dialogue with internal and external customers/stakeholders, establish common ground, and influence change
Solid planning skills to support the Leader in day-to-day operation of the business intelligence program.
Advanced analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills to identify and take action to assess needs, address challenges, and manage change
Basic leadership skills to provide day-to-day technical guidance



Beyond the role:


Community & Wellness – We recognize and respect each other’s diverse needs. We strive to maintain a healthy culture of psychological safety, belonging, and space to prioritize healthy minds and well-being. This includes Wellness Wednesday (meeting free time), flexible paid holidays, a free subscription to the Calm app, and a flexible hybrid work environment focused on connections. Our teams also enjoy giving back to the community, and having fun, whether volunteering in the community, or running together on our Sun Run team. In 2023, Technical Safety BC donated to Crisis Centre BC, Aboriginal Coalition to End Homelessness, BC Wildfire Recovery, PADS, and Rise to Thrive Foundation.
Employee Resource Groups – We have Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) for Mental Health & Wellness, Indigenous Relations & Reconciliation, and Equity Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) to support initiatives we’re passionate about.
Learning & Development – We value giving and receiving feedback, as well as encouraging different ways for us to continuously learn as a company. This can be through lessons learned, wrap up sessions, one-on-one meetings, and team or individual courses, workshops, and conferences. In addition, we offer up to $1500 tuition aid per calendar year to support your education and learning goals.
Compensation & Benefits – In full transparency, you can find our industry-competitive compensation information on our postings. For our regular employees, we have outstanding benefits that include extended health, dental and disability coverage, access to an employee and family assistance program (EFAP), competitive annual paid vacation entitlements, public service defined benefit pension plan, generous top-up allowance for new parents, and time-off for caregiving, moving, and adoption leave. We recently upgraded our mental health benefits to $1500 separate from our non-mental health paramedical services too.



About Technical Safety BC

At Technical Safety BC, we matter to each other. Together, we apply a systems mindset to safety, embrace possibility, and act on what we learn. Our culture empowers and enables innovation and connection. Our environment welcomes diverse perspectives and learning is celebrated. We make decisions based on data and use our expertise to make the safety system equitable for all. 

Our values guide our work.


We see genius in diversity
We foster confidence
We make the complex simple
We adapt



Technical Safety BC is an independent, self-funded organization that oversees the safe installation and operation of technical systems and equipment across the province. In addition to issuing permits, licenses and certificates, we work with industry to reduce safety risks through assessment, education and outreach, enforcement, and research. Through simplification of our initiatives, we promote understanding and engagement, making safety accessible to everyone. As society changes, we create and adopt new ideas, skills, and tools that will enable us to meet the safety challenges of a highly-connected world.

We see genius in diversity and are committed to creating an equitable and inclusive workforce. We recognize that diverse life paths and experiences contribute to the overall qualifications for each role. If you feel that you could excel in this position, but do not necessarily meet the formal requirements, we encourage you to apply.

If you are interested in one of our career opportunities and require accommodation or assistance with the application or recruitment process, please contact us directly at careers@technicalsafetybc.ca.

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 4:00pm PT on October 2nd, 2026. This opportunity will remain posted until filled; however, priority consideration will be given to those who apply by the deadline. To see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at Technical Safety BC, please visit our careers page.

Title: Senior Associate, Strategy & Operations - Integrity (International)
Description:
About the Team

The Integrity team is seeking a Strategy & Operations Senior Associate to help reduce fraud costs and drive solutions that safeguard the integrity of our platform. In this role, you'll develop a deep understanding of our three core audiences—Consumers, Dashers, and Merchants—and become a key resource for analyzing behaviors that may indicate risky or abusive patterns. You'll lead investigations into high-risk activity, design data-informed strategies, and implement cross-functional initiatives to mitigate losses while maintaining a seamless and trusted user experience. Most importantly, you'll help strike the right balance between user trust and risk management, ensuring we continue to support growth while protecting the platform.

About the Role

Our best Senior Associates are data-driven, truth seeking, strategic thought partners and operators. They combine business context and analytics to take on a problem area and implement a customized solution. Think this is you? Read on…

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…


Establish and refine DoorDash's strategic approach to payments, credit and refund risks - work on the operations, engineering, and analytics needed to protect DoorDash's audiences from bad actors
Analyze user behavior across DoorDash's platform – complete end-to-end analysis that allows us to better identify the bad actors and improve the experience of good users
Influence and engage across the company - partner with the product, engineering, and analytics teams to establish goals and build strategic programs
Improve through experimentation – use data-driven decision-making to run tests in order to reduce risk while accelerating growth


We're excited about you because…


2+ years of experience in consulting, strategy, business development, operations, technology, investment banking, analytics or related experience
Experience leading projects, hitting goals, and succeeding in a team environment
Strong communicator, both written and verbal
Problem solving and analytical skills, including proficiency in SQL and expertise in Excel (can maintain complex spreadsheets/sheets)
You have a bachelor's degree


Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package for all regular employees, that includes paid time off, paid parental leave, wellness benefit and several paid holidays.

Additionally, for full-time employees, DoorDash offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, disability and basic life insurance, an RRSP including an employer match, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.

$97,000—$121,000 CAD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

If you need any accommodations, please inform your recruiting contact upon initial connection.

Title: Specialist, Personal Insurance Financial Reporting & Analysis
Description:
Job Description

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Manager, PI Operational Reporting & Analysis, the Specialist, PI Financial Reporting & Analysis plays a critical role in providing timely, insightful performance reporting to support senior leaders across Personal Insurance. This role focuses heavily on the weekly presentation of current results, ensuring variances from Plan are clearly identified, investigated, and communicated to business partners.

In addition, the Specialist supports the end‑to‑end annual and quarterly Plan and forecast cycles, including the collection, aggregation, and validation of business assumptions. The analysis and insights generated by this role enable leadership to understand performance trends, identify risks and opportunities, and make effective decisions for both short‑term operations and long‑term strategic planning.

What To Expect


Lead the weekly results reporting cycle, including preparing and presenting performance updates to senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Monitor and flag deviations from Plan, providing clear, concise explanations of drivers and partnering with business teams to validate assumptions and understand emerging trends.
Support the development and maintenance of the annual Plan and forecast, including collecting, aggregating, and analyzing business inputs and assumptions.
Develop financial models and analytical tools to evaluate performance, scenario impacts, and business initiatives.
Prepare and peer-review monthly and quarterly business performance reporting for internal (senior leadership, Board) and external stakeholders (regulators, auditors, investors).
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance reporting quality, timeliness, and governance across Personal Insurance.
Support documentation updates for internal governance activities such as business continuity management and vendor risk management.
Provide timely ad‑hoc analysis to respond to emerging questions and issues raised by business stakeholders.


What You Bring


University degree in Business, Accounting, Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Actuarial or a related field.
4+ years of experience in financial reporting, planning, or business performance analysis.
Professional designations such as CPA, MBA, or CFA are considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience with financial modeling, variance analysis, and performance storytelling.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to deliver clear, concise insights to senior leadership.
Advanced proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint and SQL knowledge would be asset
Experience in P&C insurance is an asset but not required.
Exceptional analytical skills, high attention to detail, and a track record of identifying trends and key performance drivers.
Self‑motivated, proactive, and able to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.


Salary Range: $73,500 - $123,500

About Us

Actual salary for the role may vary depending on work location of the successful candidate and other factors including but not limited to, skills, education, experience, working conditions and the local labour market.

What’s in it for you?


Hybrid work schedule for most roles
Company share ownership program
Incentive Program - Eligible employees may participate in various incentive plans which are paid out at the discretion of the company and subject to individual and company performance.
Pension and savings programs, with company-matched RRSP contributions
Paid volunteer days and company matching on charitable donations
Educational resources, tuition assistance, and paid time off to study for exams

Discounts on products and services

Title: Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data
Company: BC College of Nurses and Midwives
Description:
Status: Regular, Full-Time

Work Location: Hybrid, Vancouver B.C. (a minimum of 2 days in office)

Who We Are

The British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (“BCCNM”) is the college empowered under the Health Professions and Occupations Act to regulate the practice of all licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, registered midwives, registered nurses, and registered psychiatric nurses in British Columbia. Regulation helps to protect the public by ensuring that professional care or service received by the public is competent, ethical, and meets the standards that society views as acceptable.

As western Canada’s largest health profession regulator, we believe a diverse and inclusive team enriches our efforts to protect the public. We welcome applications from all who reflect of the communities we serve and especially encourage Indigenous Peoples and members of equity-seeking groups to apply. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences bring both innovation and better outcomes to the work we do and the decisions we make.

BCCNM’s commitment to Indigenous Specific Anti-Racism

BCCNM is committed to working with Indigenous Peoples and health system partners to support Indigenous-specific anti-racist practices in the health system. As the largest health regulator in Western Canada, BCCNM has the opportunity to influence the health professionals we regulate, as well as the broader health-care system, to break the cycle of racism, and improve health outcomes for Indigenous Peoples. BCCNM has pledged to become culturally safe and anti-racist, and to support the health professionals we regulate to do the same.

What We Offer You

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 – $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. Our office is closed for the 11 statutory holidays in B.C. as well as Easter Monday and Boxing Day.

What You’ll Be Doing

The Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data plays a key role in advancing BCCNM's enterprise data strategy. Working in close collaboration and alignment with the Data Optimization Centre, the position is integral to strengthening Regulatory Policy & Programs' ability to govern, manage, analyze, and use data and content to support regulatory decision-making, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The position works to establish sustainable practices, standards, governance, and reusable solutions that improve how regulatory data and content is created, managed, shared, and used.

The position works across structured data, such as system fields, measures, reports, and analytics, and unstructured content, including case documents, correspondence, forms, evidence, templates, and knowledge resources. It translates regulatory needs into integrated data, content, reporting, governance, and process improvements while ensuring alignment with privacy, security, records management, and regulatory requirements.

Initially, the position will provide dedicated support and continuity for Professional Conduct Review (PCR) during the period it undergoes Core Regulatory Transformation (CRT). As enterprise and Data Optimization Centre priorities evolve, the position is expected to be assigned to other Regulatory Policy & Programs areas to extend successful practices, build capability, and develop reusable solutions.

Key Responsibilities Include


Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre and in collaboration with responsible SMEs, provides senior data, content and business analysis for regulatory transformation under the CRT project, ensuring project deliverables and desired outcomes related to data and content management are achieved.
In partnership with regulatory leaders and other SMEs, examines end-to-end regulatory processes, information flows, decision points, and reporting needs across structured data and supporting content; challenges assumptions and current practices; and recommends opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve regulatory processes and workflows.
On the assigned projects or operational work, translates regulatory objectives and business needs into requirements, definitions, measures, business rules, metadata, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, and implementation requirements for technical and operational teams.
Reviews and advises on cross-functional information sharing and use, balancing accessibility and operational value with privacy, confidentiality, security, culturally safe practices, records management, and regulatory obligations.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead, operationalizes Data Optimization Centre strategies and frameworks, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality standards, permissions, retention, access requirements, and issue-escalation processes.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead and in collaboration with the responsible SMEs and leaders within the Regulatory program areas, leads analysis of data and content quality (completeness, consistency, accuracy), findability, and timeliness; establishes validation and exception-management approaches; identifies root causes; and coordinates remediation with business and technical owners.
Gathers requirements and leads the design and development of operational reports, dashboards, trend analyses, forms, templates, document and content workflows, repositories, and decision-support products using reusable enterprise definitions and governed information sources.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre, partners with Information Management, Information Technology, projects teams, vendors, and system and repository owners on integration, migration, configuration, testing, releases, permissions, retention, archival, disposition, and related change activities.
Maintains and prioritizes assigned project backlogs, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies; communicates implications and recommendations to Data Optimization Centre and responsible Regulatory program area leaders; and drives work to timely resolution.
Builds sustainable organizational capability by documenting reusable methods, transferring knowledge, coaching staff and data stewards, contributing to communities of practice, and sharing lessons across regulatory areas.
Supports the Data Optimization Centre in prioritizing high-value regulatory use cases, strengthening enterprise data, content, reporting, and intelligence practices, and applying successful approaches learned from projects and assignments to other regulatory areas.
Demonstrates commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and supports organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
Fosters a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, mutual respect, teamwork, and service excellence.


Your Education & Skills


Degree in data management, information management, information systems, business analytics, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
7+ years of progressive experience in senior business analysis, data and content management, information governance, data quality, reporting and analytics, process transformation, or a related field, including experience in complex, regulated, or public-sector environments.
Demonstrated ability to lead end-to-end analysis, challenge established practices constructively, identify systemic improvements, and translate strategic and operational needs into implementable data, content, and process solutions.
Strong knowledge of data and information governance, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality, permissions, retention, access controls, lifecycle requirements, and governance decision processes.
Experience translating business and regulatory objectives into requirements, business rules, measures, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, process designs, and acceptance criteria.
Strong analytical capability, including advanced Excel skills and experience with relational databases, reporting tools, dashboards, metrics, trend analysis, and interpretation of complex operational information.
Experience with enterprise content or document management platforms, such as SharePoint or comparable repositories, including metadata, classification, permissions, search and retrieval, retention, migration, and information architecture.
Experience developing and applying quality rules, reconciliations, validation methods, and exception-management processes and coordinating root-cause remediation across business and technical teams.
Demonstrated ability to advise on cross-functional information sharing while balancing accessibility, privacy, confidentiality, security, least-privilege access, legal obligations, records requirements, and appropriate use.
Experience with system and repository integration, migration, implementation, testing, release, and transition activities in collaboration with technical teams, vendors, and information owners.
Excellent strategic thinking, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority and explain complex information concepts and recommendations to non-technical and senior audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity, document and maintain clear records of risks, issues, decisions, and backlogs;
Ability to deliver high-quality work in a project-based environment within tight timelines.
Experience building sustainable organizational capability through documentation, reusable methods, coaching, knowledge transfer, stewardship, or communities of practice.
Commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and to supporting organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
Knowledge of Canadian colonial impacts on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts and of Indigenous-specific anti-racism and related reports is an asset.
Demonstrated understanding of equity, diversity, inclusion, and cultural humility as they apply to health care and regulatory practice is an asset.


How To Apply

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 11:59pm on October 4, 2026. To apply and see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at the BC College of Nurses & Midwives, please visit our website at Careers at BCCNM.

Collection Notice

To apply for a job posting, you need to create an online account with BCCNM. As part of creating your account and submitting a job application, you will be asked to provide personal information.

The BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) collects this personal information to create and manage your online account, support its recruitment and hiring processes, and administer employee records. The legal authority for collecting this information is under section 26 British Columbia’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. If you have any questions about our privacy management practices, please contact our Privacy Office at privacy@bccnm.ca

Please note: BCCNM no longer requires staff, contractors, board and committee members, and volunteers to provide an attestation of vaccination related to the Covid-19 pandemic.

In the event of a Public Health Order being issued, the College is committed to full compliance with all directives and guidelines set forth by the Provincial Health Officer (PHO) to ensure the safety and well-being of our employees and the community partners we work with, consistent with the duty of the College to serve and protect the public.

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 – $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. Our office is closed for the 11 statutory holidays in B.C. as well as Easter Monday and Boxing Day.

What You’ll Be Doing

The Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data plays a key role in advancing BCCNM's enterprise data strategy. Working in close collaboration and alignment with the Data Optimization Centre, the position is integral to strengthening Regulatory Policy & Programs' ability to govern, manage, analyze, and use data and content to support regulatory decision-making, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The position works to establish sustainable practices, standards, governance, and reusable solutions that improve how regulatory data and content is created, managed, shared, and used.

The position works across structured data, such as system fields, measures, reports, and analytics, and unstructured content, including case documents, correspondence, forms, evidence, templates, and knowledge resources. It translates regulatory needs into integrated data, content, reporting, governance, and process improvements while ensuring alignment with privacy, security, records management, and regulatory requirements.

Initially, the position will provide dedicated support and continuity for Professional Conduct Review (PCR) during the period it undergoes Core Regulatory Transformation (CRT). As enterprise and Data Optimization Centre priorities evolve, the position is expected to be assigned to other Regulatory Policy & Programs areas to extend successful practices, build capability, and develop reusable solutions.

Key Responsibilities Include

  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre and in collaboration with responsible SMEs, provides senior data, content and business analysis for regulatory transformation under the CRT project, ensuring project deliverables and desired outcomes related to data and content management are achieved.
  • In partnership with regulatory leaders and other SMEs, examines end-to-end regulatory processes, information flows, decision points, and reporting needs across structured data and supporting content; challenges assumptions and current practices; and recommends opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve regulatory processes and workflows.
  • On the assigned projects or operational work, translates regulatory objectives and business needs into requirements, definitions, measures, business rules, metadata, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, and implementation requirements for technical and operational teams.
  • Reviews and advises on cross-functional information sharing and use, balancing accessibility and operational value with privacy, confidentiality, security, culturally safe practices, records management, and regulatory obligations.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead, operationalizes Data Optimization Centre strategies and frameworks, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality standards, permissions, retention, access requirements, and issue-escalation processes.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead and in collaboration with the responsible SMEs and leaders within the Regulatory program areas, leads analysis of data and content quality (completeness, consistency, accuracy), findability, and timeliness; establishes validation and exception-management approaches; identifies root causes; and coordinates remediation with business and technical owners.
  • Gathers requirements and leads the design and development of operational reports, dashboards, trend analyses, forms, templates, document and content workflows, repositories, and decision-support products using reusable enterprise definitions and governed information sources.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre, partners with Information Management, Information Technology, projects teams, vendors, and system and repository owners on integration, migration, configuration, testing, releases, permissions, retention, archival, disposition, and related change activities.
  • Maintains and prioritizes assigned project backlogs, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies; communicates implications and recommendations to Data Optimization Centre and responsible Regulatory program area leaders; and drives work to timely resolution.
  • Builds sustainable organizational capability by documenting reusable methods, transferring knowledge, coaching staff and data stewards, contributing to communities of practice, and sharing lessons across regulatory areas.
  • Supports the Data Optimization Centre in prioritizing high-value regulatory use cases, strengthening enterprise data, content, reporting, and intelligence practices, and applying successful approaches learned from projects and assignments to other regulatory areas.
  • Demonstrates commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and supports organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
  • Fosters a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, mutual respect, teamwork, and service excellence.

Your Education & Skills

  • Degree in data management, information management, information systems, business analytics, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in senior business analysis, data and content management, information governance, data quality, reporting and analytics, process transformation, or a related field, including experience in complex, regulated, or public-sector environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead end-to-end analysis, challenge established practices constructively, identify systemic improvements, and translate strategic and operational needs into implementable data, content, and process solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of data and information governance, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality, permissions, retention, access controls, lifecycle requirements, and governance decision processes.
  • Experience translating business and regulatory objectives into requirements, business rules, measures, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, process designs, and acceptance criteria.
  • Strong analytical capability, including advanced Excel skills and experience with relational databases, reporting tools, dashboards, metrics, trend analysis, and interpretation of complex operational information.
  • Experience with enterprise content or document management platforms, such as SharePoint or comparable repositories, including metadata, classification, permissions, search and retrieval, retention, migration, and information architecture.
  • Experience developing and applying quality rules, reconciliations, validation methods, and exception-management processes and coordinating root-cause remediation across business and technical teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to advise on cross-functional information sharing while balancing accessibility, privacy, confidentiality, security, least-privilege access, legal obligations, records requirements, and appropriate use.
  • Experience with system and repository integration, migration, implementation, testing, release, and transition activities in collaboration with technical teams, vendors, and information owners.
  • Excellent strategic thinking, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority and explain complex information concepts and recommendations to non-technical and senior audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity, document and maintain clear records of risks, issues, decisions, and backlogs;
  • Ability to deliver high-quality work in a project-based environment within tight timelines.
  • Experience building sustainable organizational capability through documentation, reusable methods, coaching, knowledge transfer, stewardship, or communities of practice.
  • Commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and to supporting organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
  • Knowledge of Canadian colonial impacts on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts and of Indigenous-specific anti-racism and related reports is an asset.
  • Demonstrated understanding of equity, diversity, inclusion, and cultural humility as they apply to health care and regulatory practice is an asset.

How To Apply

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 11:59pm on October 4, 2026. To apply and see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at the BC College of Nurses & Midwives, please visit our website at Careers at BCCNM.

To apply for a job posting, you need to create an online account with BCCNM. As part of creating your account and submitting a job application, you will be asked to provide personal information.

The BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) collects this personal information to create and manage your online account, support its recruitment and hiring processes, and administer employee records. The legal authority for collecting this information is under section 26 British Columbia’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. If you have any questions about our privacy management practices, please contact our Privacy Office at privacy@bccnm.ca

Please note: BCCNM no longer requires staff, contractors, board and committee members, and volunteers to provide an attestation of vaccination related to the Covid-19 pandemic.

In the event of a Public Health Order being issued, the College is committed to full compliance with all directives and guidelines set forth by the Provincial Health Officer (PHO) to ensure the safety and well-being of our employees and the community partners we work with, consistent with the duty of the College to serve and protect the public.

Title: Commercial Analytics and Insights Lead
Description:
We’re seeking an Analytics & Insights Lead to support complex customer and utility reporting needs while partnering with Product to design scalable, long-term solutions and shape the roadmap for our data and reporting productes. This role plays a critical part in translating bespoke reporting requests into repeatable insights and helping retire manual workflows over time.

This is a highly visible, cross-functional role working across Analytics, Product, Customer Success, and external partners—including direct interaction with customers to clarify reporting needs, explain insights, and ensure alignment on data outputs.

Key Responsibilities


Fulfill complex, short-term reporting requests for utilities and enterprise customers
Triangulate data across internal systems (e.g., platform + BI tools)
Identify patterns in ad hoc requests and document recurring needs as inputs to product requirements
Partner with Product to:
Define canonical metrics
Validate data models
Inform reporting roadmap decisions
Create interim standardized templates where possible
Improve documentation and data definitions used by internal teams
Help reduce reliance on bespoke reporting over time
Serve as a customer-facing analytics resource—responding to questions, clarifying requirements, and communicating insights in a clear, approachable way


This role is expected to evolve over time from fulfilling complex reporting requests to owning the product roadmap for standardized insights and reporting – including metric definitions and executive facing analysis – as reporting becomes productized. For the right candide, this is a path toward product management for our data products.

What Success Looks Like


Fewer “net-new” reporting requests each quarter
Faster turnaround on remaining requests
Clear documentation of metrics and definitions
Seamless handoff of repeatable insights into productized reporting
A clear, prioritized view of which reporting needs should be built into the product


Qualifications


2+ years in analytics, data science, or BI roles
2+ years in the EV Charging/eMobility space.
Strong BI experience (Domo preferred)
Experience supporting enterprise customers or external stakeholders
Comfortable working with ambiguity and imperfect data
Strong communicator—can explain data tradeoffs clearly
Demonstrated ability to handle customer-facing communication, including clarifying requests, gathering requirements, and translating technical data concepts for non-technical audiences
Interest in growing toward product management – i.e. translating recurring customer needs into product requirements – is a strong plus

Title: Compensation Analyst
Description:
We know it is our people who make us great at what we do.




We are looking for a compensation professional to support our growing compensation consulting team on several current and up coming client projects, and other initiatives. We are looking for someone, based in Vancouver or Toronto, with superb analytical and communication skills who is highly motivated, has a fine eye for detail, and can juggle multiple tasks and deliverables.




A typical day-in-the life of a Compensation Analyst involves meeting with clients, performing data analysis, understanding compensation trends to inform clients on compensation-related inquiries, and supporting internal projects. As a team member, you will work in partnership with the project managers to support clients all across Canada and gain exposure to the many areas of compensation practices including salary structure design, market analysis, job documentation and evaluation, executive pay, pay equity, salary surveys and many more!




If you are looking to take your HR and compensation career to the next level, this may be the right role for you!




This posting is for an existing vacancy that we are actively seeking to fill.




Roles and Responsibilities

Utilize Excel and other analysis tools to build compensation-related tools, dashboards, and analysis by adopting advanced techniques to compute and aggregate data, and conduct market comparisons
Interpret data and derive key market insights for clients and other reports
Support consulting team members on client projects by providing high-touch data analysis covering a wide-spread of broad compensation activities, including external market analysis using salary surveys, salary structure design, executive pay, incentive plan design, pay equity, and job evaluation
Conduct market benchmarking by reviewing client data, determining appropriate peer groups, and performing data compilation/aggregation among multiple sources, sectors, and industry databases
Collect, organize, track, and interpret client pay program information and policy material
Support national and custom external market compensation survey activities relating to questionnaire setup, create job capsules, survey tracking, database management, administration, data validation, and client communications
Help clients write job descriptions (JDs) by reviewing existing job documentation, organizational structures, JD templates, and conducting interviews
Support consultants on project management duties, including managing client documentation, coordination, scheduling, meeting note documentation, and general status tracking
Support the job evaluation process by reviewing and creating job descriptions and evaluating roles using a job evaluation methodology
Conduct research and perform financial analyses of industry sectors and client peer groups to understand business strategy, corporate performance, compensation, and rewards practices and trends
Support the team in preparation of client and business development-related presentations and executive reports; translate data into broader total rewards themes and recommendations, utilizing multiple applications including MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint




What we offer

Collaborative and engaging atmosphere
Variety in work and ability to evolve and grow your career
Working with colleagues across Canada and across multiple practice areas
Opportunities to help build and evolve our practice
Competitive compensation in terms of salary, bonus and paid vacation time (commensurate with experience)
An entrepreneurial, collegial work environment
Hybrid work style and dress for your day approach

What you offer

0-2 years of relevant experience is preferred but not required. Previous co-op terms, internships, or other related experience will be considered an asset
Bachelor's degree specifically in Business, Commerce, Economics, or a related field (required) with a baseline understanding of the different organization structures
Analytical skills and basic proficiency in MS Excel (comfortable with lookups, pivot tables, and basic formulas) combined with a strong knowledge of Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and database management
Strong oral and written communication skills including the ability to independently write a strong first draft report or insights presentation for clients
Strong desire to learn and develop through exposure to various projects and clients
Demonstrated ability to follow established standards and procedures
Ability to work in a team environment while managing multiple priorities and projects
Excellent interpersonal skills, strong verbal and written communication skills
Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
Commitment to superior client satisfaction




Strong assets but not required

Prior co-op/ internship experience in data analysis, consulting, and/or compensation
Previous work experience in compensation with knowledge in market matching and benchmarking, job evaluation, job description writing, pay equity, or executive compensation
In the process of completing or willingness to complete the Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation
Bilingual in both English and French (reading, writing, and speaking)




Who we are:

At Eckler, we are driven by our purpose to care and to do right by people so that together we can achieve a brighter, more secure future. It’s just one of the reasons Eckler has been recognized multiple times as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures. Our origins go back to 1927, making us one of Canada’s first actuarial practices. Based in Canada and the Caribbean, we’re a team of committed and highly skilled professionals consulting in the areas of pension, retirement, financial wellness, investment, group benefits, insurance, change management and communication and technology. Owned and operated by its active Principals, the company has earned a reputation for service continuity and high professional standards. Eckler is a founding member of Abelica Global – an international alliance of independent actuarial and consulting firms operating in over 20 countries.




At Eckler, we value diversity of all types. Our organization is made up of smart, collaborative, and thoughtful people with a wide range of backgrounds, skills, and experiences. We are committed to an inclusive, diverse, and accessible workplace and encourage all interested applicants to submit a cover letter and resume for consideration. Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process or those needing job postings in an alternative format may e-mail a request to careers@eckler.ca.




Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used during the recruitment process to screen or assess applications. All evaluations involving AI are reviewed by in-house recruiters prior to making any final decisions.




We thank all applicants for their interest, but only those selected for the short list will be contacted.
