Title: Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data
Company: BC College of Nurses and Midwives
Description:
Status: Regular, Full-Time

Work Location: Hybrid, Vancouver B.C. (a minimum of 2 days in office)

Who We Are

The British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (“BCCNM”) is the college empowered under the Health Professions and Occupations Act to regulate the practice of all licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, registered midwives, registered nurses, and registered psychiatric nurses in British Columbia. Regulation helps to protect the public by ensuring that professional care or service received by the public is competent, ethical, and meets the standards that society views as acceptable.

As western Canada’s largest health profession regulator, we believe a diverse and inclusive team enriches our efforts to protect the public. We welcome applications from all who reflect of the communities we serve and especially encourage Indigenous Peoples and members of equity-seeking groups to apply. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences bring both innovation and better outcomes to the work we do and the decisions we make.

BCCNM’s commitment to Indigenous Specific Anti-Racism

BCCNM is committed to working with Indigenous Peoples and health system partners to support Indigenous-specific anti-racist practices in the health system. As the largest health regulator in Western Canada, BCCNM has the opportunity to influence the health professionals we regulate, as well as the broader health-care system, to break the cycle of racism, and improve health outcomes for Indigenous Peoples. BCCNM has pledged to become culturally safe and anti-racist, and to support the health professionals we regulate to do the same.

What We Offer You

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 – $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. Our office is closed for the 11 statutory holidays in B.C. as well as Easter Monday and Boxing Day.

What You’ll Be Doing

The Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data plays a key role in advancing BCCNM's enterprise data strategy. Working in close collaboration and alignment with the Data Optimization Centre, the position is integral to strengthening Regulatory Policy & Programs' ability to govern, manage, analyze, and use data and content to support regulatory decision-making, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The position works to establish sustainable practices, standards, governance, and reusable solutions that improve how regulatory data and content is created, managed, shared, and used.

The position works across structured data, such as system fields, measures, reports, and analytics, and unstructured content, including case documents, correspondence, forms, evidence, templates, and knowledge resources. It translates regulatory needs into integrated data, content, reporting, governance, and process improvements while ensuring alignment with privacy, security, records management, and regulatory requirements.

Initially, the position will provide dedicated support and continuity for Professional Conduct Review (PCR) during the period it undergoes Core Regulatory Transformation (CRT). As enterprise and Data Optimization Centre priorities evolve, the position is expected to be assigned to other Regulatory Policy & Programs areas to extend successful practices, build capability, and develop reusable solutions.

Key Responsibilities Include


Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre and in collaboration with responsible SMEs, provides senior data, content and business analysis for regulatory transformation under the CRT project, ensuring project deliverables and desired outcomes related to data and content management are achieved.
In partnership with regulatory leaders and other SMEs, examines end-to-end regulatory processes, information flows, decision points, and reporting needs across structured data and supporting content; challenges assumptions and current practices; and recommends opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve regulatory processes and workflows.
On the assigned projects or operational work, translates regulatory objectives and business needs into requirements, definitions, measures, business rules, metadata, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, and implementation requirements for technical and operational teams.
Reviews and advises on cross-functional information sharing and use, balancing accessibility and operational value with privacy, confidentiality, security, culturally safe practices, records management, and regulatory obligations.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead, operationalizes Data Optimization Centre strategies and frameworks, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality standards, permissions, retention, access requirements, and issue-escalation processes.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead and in collaboration with the responsible SMEs and leaders within the Regulatory program areas, leads analysis of data and content quality (completeness, consistency, accuracy), findability, and timeliness; establishes validation and exception-management approaches; identifies root causes; and coordinates remediation with business and technical owners.
Gathers requirements and leads the design and development of operational reports, dashboards, trend analyses, forms, templates, document and content workflows, repositories, and decision-support products using reusable enterprise definitions and governed information sources.
Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre, partners with Information Management, Information Technology, projects teams, vendors, and system and repository owners on integration, migration, configuration, testing, releases, permissions, retention, archival, disposition, and related change activities.
Maintains and prioritizes assigned project backlogs, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies; communicates implications and recommendations to Data Optimization Centre and responsible Regulatory program area leaders; and drives work to timely resolution.
Builds sustainable organizational capability by documenting reusable methods, transferring knowledge, coaching staff and data stewards, contributing to communities of practice, and sharing lessons across regulatory areas.
Supports the Data Optimization Centre in prioritizing high-value regulatory use cases, strengthening enterprise data, content, reporting, and intelligence practices, and applying successful approaches learned from projects and assignments to other regulatory areas.
Demonstrates commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and supports organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
Fosters a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, mutual respect, teamwork, and service excellence.


Your Education & Skills


Degree in data management, information management, information systems, business analytics, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
7+ years of progressive experience in senior business analysis, data and content management, information governance, data quality, reporting and analytics, process transformation, or a related field, including experience in complex, regulated, or public-sector environments.
Demonstrated ability to lead end-to-end analysis, challenge established practices constructively, identify systemic improvements, and translate strategic and operational needs into implementable data, content, and process solutions.
Strong knowledge of data and information governance, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality, permissions, retention, access controls, lifecycle requirements, and governance decision processes.
Experience translating business and regulatory objectives into requirements, business rules, measures, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, process designs, and acceptance criteria.
Strong analytical capability, including advanced Excel skills and experience with relational databases, reporting tools, dashboards, metrics, trend analysis, and interpretation of complex operational information.
Experience with enterprise content or document management platforms, such as SharePoint or comparable repositories, including metadata, classification, permissions, search and retrieval, retention, migration, and information architecture.
Experience developing and applying quality rules, reconciliations, validation methods, and exception-management processes and coordinating root-cause remediation across business and technical teams.
Demonstrated ability to advise on cross-functional information sharing while balancing accessibility, privacy, confidentiality, security, least-privilege access, legal obligations, records requirements, and appropriate use.
Experience with system and repository integration, migration, implementation, testing, release, and transition activities in collaboration with technical teams, vendors, and information owners.
Excellent strategic thinking, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority and explain complex information concepts and recommendations to non-technical and senior audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity, document and maintain clear records of risks, issues, decisions, and backlogs;
Ability to deliver high-quality work in a project-based environment within tight timelines.
Experience building sustainable organizational capability through documentation, reusable methods, coaching, knowledge transfer, stewardship, or communities of practice.
Commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and to supporting organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
Knowledge of Canadian colonial impacts on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts and of Indigenous-specific anti-racism and related reports is an asset.
Demonstrated understanding of equity, diversity, inclusion, and cultural humility as they apply to health care and regulatory practice is an asset.


How To Apply

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 11:59pm on October 4, 2026. To apply and see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at the BC College of Nurses & Midwives, please visit our website at Careers at BCCNM.

Collection Notice

To apply for a job posting, you need to create an online account with BCCNM. As part of creating your account and submitting a job application, you will be asked to provide personal information.

The BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) collects this personal information to create and manage your online account, support its recruitment and hiring processes, and administer employee records. The legal authority for collecting this information is under section 26 British Columbia’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. If you have any questions about our privacy management practices, please contact our Privacy Office at privacy@bccnm.ca

Please note: BCCNM no longer requires staff, contractors, board and committee members, and volunteers to provide an attestation of vaccination related to the Covid-19 pandemic.

In the event of a Public Health Order being issued, the College is committed to full compliance with all directives and guidelines set forth by the Provincial Health Officer (PHO) to ensure the safety and well-being of our employees and the community partners we work with, consistent with the duty of the College to serve and protect the public.

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 – $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. Our office is closed for the 11 statutory holidays in B.C. as well as Easter Monday and Boxing Day.

What You’ll Be Doing

The Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data plays a key role in advancing BCCNM's enterprise data strategy. Working in close collaboration and alignment with the Data Optimization Centre, the position is integral to strengthening Regulatory Policy & Programs' ability to govern, manage, analyze, and use data and content to support regulatory decision-making, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The position works to establish sustainable practices, standards, governance, and reusable solutions that improve how regulatory data and content is created, managed, shared, and used.

The position works across structured data, such as system fields, measures, reports, and analytics, and unstructured content, including case documents, correspondence, forms, evidence, templates, and knowledge resources. It translates regulatory needs into integrated data, content, reporting, governance, and process improvements while ensuring alignment with privacy, security, records management, and regulatory requirements.

Initially, the position will provide dedicated support and continuity for Professional Conduct Review (PCR) during the period it undergoes Core Regulatory Transformation (CRT). As enterprise and Data Optimization Centre priorities evolve, the position is expected to be assigned to other Regulatory Policy & Programs areas to extend successful practices, build capability, and develop reusable solutions.

Key Responsibilities Include

  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre and in collaboration with responsible SMEs, provides senior data, content and business analysis for regulatory transformation under the CRT project, ensuring project deliverables and desired outcomes related to data and content management are achieved.
  • In partnership with regulatory leaders and other SMEs, examines end-to-end regulatory processes, information flows, decision points, and reporting needs across structured data and supporting content; challenges assumptions and current practices; and recommends opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve regulatory processes and workflows.
  • On the assigned projects or operational work, translates regulatory objectives and business needs into requirements, definitions, measures, business rules, metadata, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, and implementation requirements for technical and operational teams.
  • Reviews and advises on cross-functional information sharing and use, balancing accessibility and operational value with privacy, confidentiality, security, culturally safe practices, records management, and regulatory obligations.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead, operationalizes Data Optimization Centre strategies and frameworks, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality standards, permissions, retention, access requirements, and issue-escalation processes.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre Lead and in collaboration with the responsible SMEs and leaders within the Regulatory program areas, leads analysis of data and content quality (completeness, consistency, accuracy), findability, and timeliness; establishes validation and exception-management approaches; identifies root causes; and coordinates remediation with business and technical owners.
  • Gathers requirements and leads the design and development of operational reports, dashboards, trend analyses, forms, templates, document and content workflows, repositories, and decision-support products using reusable enterprise definitions and governed information sources.
  • Under the direction of the Data Optimization Centre, partners with Information Management, Information Technology, projects teams, vendors, and system and repository owners on integration, migration, configuration, testing, releases, permissions, retention, archival, disposition, and related change activities.
  • Maintains and prioritizes assigned project backlogs, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies; communicates implications and recommendations to Data Optimization Centre and responsible Regulatory program area leaders; and drives work to timely resolution.
  • Builds sustainable organizational capability by documenting reusable methods, transferring knowledge, coaching staff and data stewards, contributing to communities of practice, and sharing lessons across regulatory areas.
  • Supports the Data Optimization Centre in prioritizing high-value regulatory use cases, strengthening enterprise data, content, reporting, and intelligence practices, and applying successful approaches learned from projects and assignments to other regulatory areas.
  • Demonstrates commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and supports organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
  • Fosters a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, mutual respect, teamwork, and service excellence.

Your Education & Skills

  • Degree in data management, information management, information systems, business analytics, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in senior business analysis, data and content management, information governance, data quality, reporting and analytics, process transformation, or a related field, including experience in complex, regulated, or public-sector environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead end-to-end analysis, challenge established practices constructively, identify systemic improvements, and translate strategic and operational needs into implementable data, content, and process solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of data and information governance, including ownership and stewardship, business definitions, metadata, taxonomy, classification, lineage, quality, permissions, retention, access controls, lifecycle requirements, and governance decision processes.
  • Experience translating business and regulatory objectives into requirements, business rules, measures, content models, workflows, reporting specifications, process designs, and acceptance criteria.
  • Strong analytical capability, including advanced Excel skills and experience with relational databases, reporting tools, dashboards, metrics, trend analysis, and interpretation of complex operational information.
  • Experience with enterprise content or document management platforms, such as SharePoint or comparable repositories, including metadata, classification, permissions, search and retrieval, retention, migration, and information architecture.
  • Experience developing and applying quality rules, reconciliations, validation methods, and exception-management processes and coordinating root-cause remediation across business and technical teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to advise on cross-functional information sharing while balancing accessibility, privacy, confidentiality, security, least-privilege access, legal obligations, records requirements, and appropriate use.
  • Experience with system and repository integration, migration, implementation, testing, release, and transition activities in collaboration with technical teams, vendors, and information owners.
  • Excellent strategic thinking, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority and explain complex information concepts and recommendations to non-technical and senior audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity, document and maintain clear records of risks, issues, decisions, and backlogs;
  • Ability to deliver high-quality work in a project-based environment within tight timelines.
  • Experience building sustainable organizational capability through documentation, reusable methods, coaching, knowledge transfer, stewardship, or communities of practice.
  • Commitment to ongoing learning related to Indigenous cultural safety and humility and to supporting organizational action to address Indigenous-specific racism in BC’s health care system.
  • Knowledge of Canadian colonial impacts on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts and of Indigenous-specific anti-racism and related reports is an asset.
  • Demonstrated understanding of equity, diversity, inclusion, and cultural humility as they apply to health care and regulatory practice is an asset.

How To Apply

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 11:59pm on October 4, 2026. To apply and see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at the BC College of Nurses & Midwives, please visit our website at Careers at BCCNM.

To apply for a job posting, you need to create an online account with BCCNM. As part of creating your account and submitting a job application, you will be asked to provide personal information.

The BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) collects this personal information to create and manage your online account, support its recruitment and hiring processes, and administer employee records. The legal authority for collecting this information is under section 26 British Columbia’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. If you have any questions about our privacy management practices, please contact our Privacy Office at privacy@bccnm.ca

Please note: BCCNM no longer requires staff, contractors, board and committee members, and volunteers to provide an attestation of vaccination related to the Covid-19 pandemic.

In the event of a Public Health Order being issued, the College is committed to full compliance with all directives and guidelines set forth by the Provincial Health Officer (PHO) to ensure the safety and well-being of our employees and the community partners we work with, consistent with the duty of the College to serve and protect the public.

Title: Data Analytics Consultant

Ready to take your career to the next level? Invest in yourself! MSP Corp is a dynamic and evolving organization.  Our team is energetic and multidisciplinary, performing at the highest levels.  We thrive on the diversity of our team and believe that any candidate could be the talent to take us to the next level. As we continue to grow, we are seeking a Data Analytics Consultant to join our West team. 




About the Role   




As an experienced Data Analytics Consultant this individual will work as part of our data analytics team, supporting clients with requirements gathering, prototyping, development, and support. Client scenarios range in complexity. This individual must have a good blend of people, functional, and technical skills for cross-team collaboration and support. We are looking for individuals who will interface with multiple business and technology stakeholders and teams to evaluate and improve existing processes using multiple technology platforms. 





Location: Canada


Schedule: Monday to Friday, 40 hours per week, 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. 


Work Mode: Remote













What You Will Do  





Architecting, designing, and developing end to end analytical data solutions from source raw data all the way to Power BI front end

Working with business/project team members to understand the requirements 


Defining BI framework model, semantic layers and Metadata repositories to support reporting and administration 


Developing and managing BI end user presentation layer training and documentation. 


Technical documentation 


Supporting business development efforts (proposals and client presentations) 


Estimating effort for development and support engagements in Data Engineering and related technologies 


Status reporting 


Interacting with various client and management stake holders to get the work completed 


You would represent the company in the market and must reflect the core values of the company which include: 


Continuous improvement as a way of life 


Fair and generous relationships with our people and customers 


Certifications helpful to role: 






Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals 


Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Fundamentals 


Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals 


Microsoft Certified: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals 


Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate 


Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Scientist Associate 


Azure Databricks Data Engineer Associate - Certifications





Microsoft Certified: SQL AI Developer Associate
















What We Are Looking For  





5+ years hands-on experience in Microsoft Data Stack incl. SQL Server, data warehousing, MS Fabric/Data Bricks


3+ years hands-on experience in Microsoft BI Stack incl. Power BI, SSAS, SSRS, SSIS 


Proficiency in the development and administration of at least one of the following areas: 


Back end data integration and architecture including dimensional data modeling, database design, data warehousing, ETL development (e.g. ADF), and performance tuning, front-end reporting and analytics platforms including OLAP cube design, tabular data modeling.


Strong Data Modeling skills for Star-Schema 


Strong Programming skills in T-SQL, Spark (PySpark, SQL, Scala, etc), DAX, Power Query 


Strong analytical thinking for translating data into informative visuals and reports 


Experience developing visual reports including custom visuals, dashboards and KPI scorecards using Power BI 


The ability to implement row level security on data and have an understanding of application security layer models in the data platforms of SQL Server, Azure, MS Fabric and Power BI 


Foundational knowledge of the following areas: Metadata Management; Master Data Management; Data Governance; Data Analytics 


Good understanding of AI fundamentals.


Certifications required: 


-Microsoft Certified: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate


-Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate


Strong written and verbal communications skills 













Why Work at MSP Corp  





Benefits package. 


Dynamic work environment. 


Corporate gym discounts. 


Wellness day. 


Opportunities for growth and training. 













Ready to make a difference? Join us and shape the future. Apply today!  




Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: At MSP Corp, we believe that diversity, equity, and inclusion are essential for fostering a healthy and innovative work environment. We are committed to creating a workplace where everyone, regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, ability, or any other characteristic, feels valued and respected. We encourage applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and perspectives and ensure a fair and inclusive recruitment process.  




Thank you for your interest in this opportunity. We will only contact candidates whose profile closely matches the job requirements.

Title: Compensation Analyst
Description:
We know it is our people who make us great at what we do.




We are looking for a compensation professional to support our growing compensation consulting team on several current and up coming client projects, and other initiatives. We are looking for someone, based in Vancouver or Toronto, with superb analytical and communication skills who is highly motivated, has a fine eye for detail, and can juggle multiple tasks and deliverables.




A typical day-in-the life of a Compensation Analyst involves meeting with clients, performing data analysis, understanding compensation trends to inform clients on compensation-related inquiries, and supporting internal projects. As a team member, you will work in partnership with the project managers to support clients all across Canada and gain exposure to the many areas of compensation practices including salary structure design, market analysis, job documentation and evaluation, executive pay, pay equity, salary surveys and many more!




If you are looking to take your HR and compensation career to the next level, this may be the right role for you!




This posting is for an existing vacancy that we are actively seeking to fill.




Roles and Responsibilities

Utilize Excel and other analysis tools to build compensation-related tools, dashboards, and analysis by adopting advanced techniques to compute and aggregate data, and conduct market comparisons
Interpret data and derive key market insights for clients and other reports
Support consulting team members on client projects by providing high-touch data analysis covering a wide-spread of broad compensation activities, including external market analysis using salary surveys, salary structure design, executive pay, incentive plan design, pay equity, and job evaluation
Conduct market benchmarking by reviewing client data, determining appropriate peer groups, and performing data compilation/aggregation among multiple sources, sectors, and industry databases
Collect, organize, track, and interpret client pay program information and policy material
Support national and custom external market compensation survey activities relating to questionnaire setup, create job capsules, survey tracking, database management, administration, data validation, and client communications
Help clients write job descriptions (JDs) by reviewing existing job documentation, organizational structures, JD templates, and conducting interviews
Support consultants on project management duties, including managing client documentation, coordination, scheduling, meeting note documentation, and general status tracking
Support the job evaluation process by reviewing and creating job descriptions and evaluating roles using a job evaluation methodology
Conduct research and perform financial analyses of industry sectors and client peer groups to understand business strategy, corporate performance, compensation, and rewards practices and trends
Support the team in preparation of client and business development-related presentations and executive reports; translate data into broader total rewards themes and recommendations, utilizing multiple applications including MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint




What we offer

Collaborative and engaging atmosphere
Variety in work and ability to evolve and grow your career
Working with colleagues across Canada and across multiple practice areas
Opportunities to help build and evolve our practice
Competitive compensation in terms of salary, bonus and paid vacation time (commensurate with experience)
An entrepreneurial, collegial work environment
Hybrid work style and dress for your day approach

What you offer

0-2 years of relevant experience is preferred but not required. Previous co-op terms, internships, or other related experience will be considered an asset
Bachelor's degree specifically in Business, Commerce, Economics, or a related field (required) with a baseline understanding of the different organization structures
Analytical skills and basic proficiency in MS Excel (comfortable with lookups, pivot tables, and basic formulas) combined with a strong knowledge of Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and database management
Strong oral and written communication skills including the ability to independently write a strong first draft report or insights presentation for clients
Strong desire to learn and develop through exposure to various projects and clients
Demonstrated ability to follow established standards and procedures
Ability to work in a team environment while managing multiple priorities and projects
Excellent interpersonal skills, strong verbal and written communication skills
Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
Commitment to superior client satisfaction




Strong assets but not required

Prior co-op/ internship experience in data analysis, consulting, and/or compensation
Previous work experience in compensation with knowledge in market matching and benchmarking, job evaluation, job description writing, pay equity, or executive compensation
In the process of completing or willingness to complete the Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation
Bilingual in both English and French (reading, writing, and speaking)




Who we are:

At Eckler, we are driven by our purpose to care and to do right by people so that together we can achieve a brighter, more secure future. It’s just one of the reasons Eckler has been recognized multiple times as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures. Our origins go back to 1927, making us one of Canada’s first actuarial practices. Based in Canada and the Caribbean, we’re a team of committed and highly skilled professionals consulting in the areas of pension, retirement, financial wellness, investment, group benefits, insurance, change management and communication and technology. Owned and operated by its active Principals, the company has earned a reputation for service continuity and high professional standards. Eckler is a founding member of Abelica Global – an international alliance of independent actuarial and consulting firms operating in over 20 countries.




At Eckler, we value diversity of all types. Our organization is made up of smart, collaborative, and thoughtful people with a wide range of backgrounds, skills, and experiences. We are committed to an inclusive, diverse, and accessible workplace and encourage all interested applicants to submit a cover letter and resume for consideration. Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process or those needing job postings in an alternative format may e-mail a request to careers@eckler.ca.




Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used during the recruitment process to screen or assess applications. All evaluations involving AI are reviewed by in-house recruiters prior to making any final decisions.




We thank all applicants for their interest, but only those selected for the short list will be contacted.
